correctness.rationale: The defining surjective majority C-coloring requires h=floor(n/2) same-colored neighbors because each crown vertex has n-1 neighbors. A nonempty color must meet each shore in at least h points, hence every class has at least 2h vertices; for n>=6 this excludes three colors. The explicit bipartition-index construction reaches two colors. For even n=2r, each class has r vertices on each shore and same-color deleted matched pairs are impossible; therefore T is the complement of S and the labeled count is binom(n,r). For odd n=2r+1, shore counts lie in {r,r+1}; a common index forces (r+1,r+1,1), yielding exactly the four stated profiles. Direct independent neighborhood enumeration, with surjectivity enforced, found counts 20,350,70,1512 at n=6,7,8,9 and exactly the claimed occupancy profiles. Finite checks do not establish the universal bound, which is analytic.
